result.topic_en: Gauss computes the total force and torque that a closed current circuit (elements da, db, dc at point (a,b,c)) exerts on a distribution of magnetic masses dm, and shows that the three force integrals vanish under the stated assumption, before expanding the torque integral.
result.transcription:
$\int X dm,\ \int Y dm,\ \int Z dm,\ \int (zY - yZ) dm,\ \int (xZ - zX) dm,$
$\int (yX - xY) dm$ [-=-].
abc = c [?]
Es ist $(x-a)^2 + (y-b)^2 + (z-c)^2 = rr$ gesetzt
[diagram: Y vorn rechts, Z oben, X links vorn]
$X = S\, \frac{\overset{(y-b)}{y}dc - \overset{(z-c)}{z}db}{r^3}$
$Y = S\, \frac{z da - x dc}{r^3}$
$Z = S\, \frac{x db - y da}{r^3}$

also $\int X dm = \int S. \frac{(y-b)dc - (z-c)db}{r^3}.dm$
$= S\, dc. \int \frac{y-b}{r^3} dm - [-dS-] S\, db. \int \frac{z-c}{r^3}.dm$
also = 0 vermöge Voraussetzung
Eben so $\int Y dm = 0,\ \int Z dm = 0$
Welches die drei ersten Bedingungen sind
Ferner $\int (yX - xY).dm = \int S \left( \frac{(y-b)y + (x-a)x}{r^3} dc - \frac{(z-c)x da - (z-c) y db}{r^3} \right) dm$
{+Was hier unter dem Integralzeichen steht, wird so verwandelt+}
$= \int S \left( \frac{(x-a)x + (y-b)y + (z-c)z}{r^3} dc - \frac{z-c}{r^3}(x da + y db + z dc) \right) dm$
$= \int S \left[ \frac{(x-a)^2 + (y-b)^2 + (z-c)^2 + a(x-a) + b(y-b) + c(z-c)}{r^3} dc \right] dm$
$- \int S\, z \frac{(x-a)da + (y-b)db + (z-c)dc}{r^3} dm$
$- \int S\, \frac{z}{r^3}(a da + b db + c dc)\, dm$
$+ \int S\, \frac{c(x da + y db + z dc)}{r^3} dm$ $\Big\} = - \int S \frac{z-c}{r^3}(a da + b db + c dc) dm + \int S \frac{c((x-a)da + (y-b)db + (z-c)dc)}{r^3} dm$
[-$= \int S \frac{dm}{r}.dc$-]
oder $\int \frac{x-a}{r^3}.dm = \xi$ gesetzt u.c. $\int \frac{dm}{r} = V$
